hypotheses.reasoning: Earliest anomaly in the login path is auth-svc's calls to the third-party identity provider (https://idp.example/oauth2/token) slowing down at 05:39:12 (4.5s, then 11s, then 13s), then timing out at 30s from 05:40:43. account-svc's AuthClient.issueToken calls time out on the same traces (t-5812, t-5823, t-5827). That fills account-svc's connection pool to auth-svc (50/50, queue growing from 30 to 101), leads to pool checkout timeouts, and edge-proxy returns 503s on POST /login starting 05:42:30. No deploy or config change shows up. The disk warning, GC pause and 429 throttling are unrelated noise.

The same chain viewed as a dependency timeout. A slow upstream combined with a 30s timeout and no circuit breaker held account-svc's pool connections long enough to empty it. Which label fits depends on whether the IdP degradation counts as a provider outage or as a slow dependency.
Pool saturation and queueing in account-svc spread the failure to edge-proxy. This is a symptom of the upstream problem, not its source.

verdict.recommendedAction: Check the identity provider's status page or open a ticket with them, and escalate to the vendor. In auth-svc, cut the IdP call timeout well below 30s and add a circuit breaker so it fails fast, with cached or degraded token issuance if possible. In account-svc, bound the auth-svc pool queue and its timeouts so slow calls can't take every connection. Watch the 503 rate on POST /login until the IdP's response times are back to normal.
